title: Case Study: WhatsApp / Chat Application
summary: Design a global, end-to-end encrypted messaging service like WhatsApp or Facebook Messenger handling 50 billion messages a day with sub-second delivery latency.

explanation.overview: A messaging application like WhatsApp requires persistent, bidirectional communication between the client and the server. Unlike standard REST APIs where the client always initiates a pull request, chat apps must push messages to receivers instantly. The core technologies involved are WebSockets, Session Servers to track which user is connected to which node, and Message Queues to handle offline user delivery.
explanation.how_it_works_internally: INTERNAL Mechanics: When User A opens WhatsApp, they establish a stateful WebSocket connection to a Chat Server. A 'Session Service' (backed by Redis) records that 'User A is on Chat Server #44'. When User A sends a message to User B, Chat Server #44 queries the Session Service to find User B. If User B is connected to Chat Server #89, the message is routed directly to Server #89 via a Pub/Sub queue, which instantly pushes it via WebSocket to User B. If User B is offline, the message is queued in Cassandra until they reconnect.

step_by_step.title: Connection Establishment
step_by_step.detail: Client negotiates a TLS WebSocket connection with the API Gateway, which routes them to a continuously running Chat Server node.

step_by_step.title: Routing Messages
step_by_step.detail: The Chat Server looks up the recipient's current active TCP connection in the global Session Store (Redis KV store).

step_by_step.title: Delivering & Acknowledging
step_by_step.detail: Message sent to recipient. Once received, an 'Ack' (double-tick) is routed back to the sender using the same infrastructure.

step_by_step.title: Offline Handling
step_by_step.detail: If recipient is offline, the message is stored in NoSQL (Cassandra). When the user connects, their client pulls pending messages and deletes them from the server (ephemeral storage).

key_concepts.definition: INTERNAL: A protocol providing full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection. Once established, both client and server can send frames simultaneously without HTTP header overhead.
The server never sees plaintext messages. The sender encrypts the payload using the receiver's public key (Signal Protocol). The server only routes the encrypted blob.

examples.title: Python Implementation Snippet: WebSocket Server
examples.description: Concrete Python code using Asyncio and WebSockets for high-concurrency connections.
examples.code:
import asyncio
import websockets

connected_users = {}

async def chat_handler(websocket, path):
    user_id = path.strip('/')
    connected_users[user_id] = websocket
    try:
        async for message in websocket:
            # Parse recipient from payload (simplified)
            target_id, payload = message.split(':', 1)
            if target_id in connected_users:
                # Push to target
                await connected_users[target_id].send(f"From {user_id}: {payload}")
            else:
                # Offline handling: save to DB
                pass
    finally:
        del connected_users[user_id]

examples.title: Decision Matrix & Tradeoffs: WebSockets vs Long Polling
examples.code:
OPTION WebSockets vs OPTION Long Polling
----------------------------------------
Pros WebSockets: True bidirectional flow, very low latency (ms), low overhead per message.
Cons WebSockets: Hard to scale load balancers (sticky sessions required), harder to deploy seamlessly.
Pros Long Polling: Uses standard HTTP infrastructure, easy to proxy.
Cons Long Polling: Header overhead (auth cookies) sent repeatedly, higher latency.

configurable_params.name: Library Configuration Parameters (OS TCP Stack)
configurable_params.default: Linux default limits `fs.file-max` heavily limit open sockets.
configurable_params.effect: Modify parameter `ulimit -n 1000000` to allow a single WhatsApp server to hold 1 million simultaneous TCP connections. Also modify `net.ipv4.tcp_rmem` (TCP buffers) to use minimal memory per connection.
configurable_params.tradeoff: Shrinking buffers allows millions of connections but penalizes high-bandwidth payloads like video transfers.

advanced_tweaks.how: Stateful Connections. Unlike standard REST apps, Chat Servers hold state (the open TCP socket). To scale this safely, the API Gateway uses Consistent Hashing by UserID to route returning clients to the same server if a connection drops.

  Bob[Bob Client] <-->|WebSocket| CS2[Chat Server 2]

limitations: Group Chats: In a 256-person group, one message requires 256 outbound WebSocket writes. If 1,000 groups chat simultaneously, it causes explosive fan-out latency. TWEAK: Implement a dedicated Group Message Dispatch service built on Erlang/Elixir (WhatsApp's actual tech stack) designed for microscopic thread concurrency.

Media Transfer: Pushing a 50MB video through WebSockets blocks the single thread parsing it. TWEAK: Upload videos via standard REST HTTP to S3, and only push the S3 URL (metadata thumbnail) over the WebSocket.

technologies_used.details: WhatsApp's original core architecture was built on Erlang (and FreeBSD) because Erlang's lightweight processes and Actor model allow millions of concurrent chat sessions per single physical server.

Used for offline message queueing. It handles ultra-fast writes (when the sender transmits) and ultra-fast deletes (when the receiver downloads). Cassandra relies on log-structured merge trees perfectly suited for this workload.
